albums.name: Nectar
albums.wiki: Nectar is the second studio album by Joji, following his successful debut record, BALLADS 1, released in October of 2018. After initially announcing a July 2020 release date, Joji postponed the album to September 25, 2020 in response to the COVID-19 pandemic and the Black Lives Matter protests. The album boasts a variety of featured singers, rappers, and producers, including: Diplo, Omar Apollo, Lil Yachty, rei brown, BENEE, and Yves Tumor. The first single from the record, “Sanctuary,” was released on June 14, 2019. The record’s second single, “Run,” released on February 7, 2020. The third single (The more streamed and popular one amongst the four), “Gimme Love,” was released on April 16, 2020, along with the announcement of the title of the album and that it was originally intended to be released on July 10, 2020. The fourth single, a collaboration with Diplo called “Daylight,” was released on August 6, 2020. The album takes a sonically different approach from "BALLADS 1", with a sound that’s less focused on Joji’s typical melancholy, lo-fi sound. Instead, the album takes a mix of many retroelements instrumentation from older Joji projects that never got to see the light of streaming services. Read more on Last.fm. albums.name: NO HANDS
albums.wiki: NO HANDS is the second independent album from alternative rap duo Joey Valence & Brae. The title of this album is a double entendre playing on the concept of “no hands” meaning to do something effortlessly and skillfully that you don’t even need hands, but also doing so with no “hands” as in violence – indicated by JVB’s shirts in the album cover. Lyrically this album explores concepts from confidence, rebellion, violence, and authenticity. In an Instagram post, JVB adds some context to this. “This album forces you to be confident in yourself and do things simply because they make you happy … building something on our own and talking our shiii while we do it. We make fun of people with false confidence and comend those who are genuine and free … love yourself, be genuine, and remember to not take yourself or life too seriously.“ This album further embraces the modernization of old school hip-hop sounds whilst simultaneously serving as a marker of maturity from them lyrically and professionally. Featuring three more diverse artists: Danny Brown, Z-Trip, and TERROR REID. Read more on Last.fm. tracklist.title: We Don't Believe What's on TV

albums.wiki: Blurryface is the fourth studio album by American musical duo Twenty One Pilots. It was released on May 17, 2015, through Fueled by Ramen. The album is primarily an alternative hip hop, electropop, and reggae album with influences of hip hop, rock, and pop. Lyrically, the album incorporates themes of mental health, doubt, and religion. It contains the successful singles "Stressed Out" and "Ride", both of which reached the top-five on the US Billboard Hot 100. Blurryface was well-received by critics, who complimented its themes and musical diversity. It is considered to be the band's breakthrough album, becoming their first and only release to reach number one on the Billboard 200, thus far. The album has sold over 1.5 million copies in the United States as of April 2017. In 2018, Blurryface became the first album in the digital era to have every track receive at least a gold certification from the Recording Industry Association of America. On May 17, 2019, it reached the milestone of being on the Billboard 200 chart for four consecutive years, never leaving the chart up until that point. It is also the most-streamed rock album in history, with over 5.8 billion plays. Read more on Last.fm. albums.name: Trench
albums.wiki: Trench is the fifth studio album by American musical duo Twenty One Pilots, released on October 5, 2018 through Fueled by Ramen. It is the band's first studio album in three years, after the breakthrough success of their previous album, Blurryface (2015). Recorded in secret during a year-long public silence, it is a concept album which explores mental health, suicide and doubt, themes prominently featured in the band's previous works, framed in the metaphorical city of Dema and the surrounding valley known as "Trench". The album is also the first release of the newly revived Elektra Music Group. The album was preceded by the release of four singles. The first two, "Jumpsuit" and "Nico and the Niners", were both released on July 11, 2018. The third single, "Levitate", was released on August 8, 2018. The fourth single, "My Blood", was released August 27, 2018. The fifth single, "Chlorine", was released January 22, 2019. To promote the album, The Bandito Tour began at the Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tennessee on October 16, 2018, and continued through June 30, 2019, ending at the Nationwide Arena in Columbus, Ohio. albums.name: BRAT

tracklist.title: I think about it all the time

albums.wiki: BRAT is the sixth studio album by Charli xcx, released on June 7, 2024, via Atlantic Records. It features an aggressive and confrontational style, yet is noted for its lyrical vulnerability. Inspired by the illegal London rave scene where Charli began her career, the album is her first release after renewing her contract with Atlantic Records in 2023. The album's sound includes elements of EDM, hyperpop and dance, creating a unique minimalism that is loud and bold. Critics have compared its sound to early 2000s Ministry of Sound compilations, describing the lyrics as both "shady and bratty" yet "tender and heartbreaking". The album explores various themes, including Charli's contentious relationship with a fellow female artist and society's fascination with "mean girls". Additionally, one track delves into her grief over the death of SOPHIE, adding a deeply personal layer to the record. At the 67th Annual Grammy Awards, Brat won Best Dance/Electronic Album and Best Recording Package awards and the first single of the album, Von Dutch won Best Pop Dance Recording. albums.wiki: Clancy is the seventh LP and fifth studio album by American musical duo Twenty One Pilots. It was released on May 24, 2024, through Fueled by Ramen. A concept record titled after the protagonist of the duo's fifth LP Trench (2018), Clancy is set to conclude the titular character's story, as established in Trench and their sixth LP, Scaled and Icy (2021). The album's lead single, "Overcompensate", was released on February 29, 2024. Read more on Last.fm. albums.name: Selected Ambient Works 85-92
albums.wiki: Selected Ambient Works 85-92 is the debut studio album by Aphex Twin, the pseudonym of British electronic musician Richard D. James. It was released on November 9, 1992 through Apollo Records, a subsidiary of Belgian label R&S Records. The album consists of beat-orientated ambient tracks recorded onto cassette reputedly dating as far back as 1985, when James was thirteen to fourteen years old. An analogue remaster of the album was released in 2006, followed by a digital remaster in 2008. Upon its release, Selected Ambient Works 85-92 received widespread acclaim, and has been considered a landmark in the fields of electronica, ambient techno, and intelligent dance music. James followed up the album in 1994 with the more traditionally ambient Selected Ambient Works Volume II. In 2012, it was named the greatest album of the 1990s by Fact. It entered the UK Dance Albums Chart at number 30 after the release of Aphex Twin's 2014 album Syro. Simon Reynolds, writing in the 1994 Spin Alternative Record Guide, gave the album a 9 rating. In 2012, Reynolds wrote that the album "infuses everyday life with a perpetual first flush of spring." John Bush of AllMusic described the album as "one of the indisputable classics of electronica, and a defining document for ambient music in particular." Reviewing the album after it was reissued by PIAS America in 2002, Rolling Stone's Pat Blashill called it a "gorgeous, ethereal album" in which James "proved that techno could be more than druggy dance music." David M. Pecoraro of Pitchfork noted "the creeping basslines, the constantly mutating drum patterns, the synth tones which moved with all the grace and fluidity of a professional dancer," describing the album as "among the most interesting music ever created with a keyboard and a computer" despite its "primitive origins". Widely regarded by critics as one of the pioneering works in early IDM and modern electronic music, retrospective reviews mention its influence on electronic artists. In 2003, the album was placed number 92 in NME's 100 Best Albums poll. The album was also featured in the book 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die. AllMusic called it "a masterpiece of ambient techno, the genre's second work of brilliance after the Orb's Adventures Beyond the Ultraworld". In 2017, Pitchfork named it the best IDM album of All-Time. Read more on Last.fm. User-contributed text is available under the Creative Commons By-SA License; additional terms may apply.
